A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HOPE-SSM research despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison; the new Appendix C in v2 shifts subsequent appendix letters.

before.justification: v1 reports original sCIFAR-10, noise-padded sCIFAR-10, and LRA results, together with numerical experiments on Hankel ranks and perturbations in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendices F and H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports revised HOPE-SSM LRA results with five-seed statistics in Table 1. Supplementary numerical and memory experiments remain in Appendices G and I.

M1.justification: The Hankel Markov-parameter representation, bilinear transformation, transfer-function sampling, and FFT computation remain the same. Algorithm 1 documents the existing Equation (7) procedure; explicitly listing the trainable sampling period does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use sCIFAR-10, its noise-padded variant, and the same six LRA tasks. The random-matrix experiments and sampling-period scenarios are also retained; no dataset or task coverage is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Liquid S4 and S5 as evaluated comparators. DSS, S4++, Regularized S4D, Spectral SSM, S4, and S4D remain with unchanged scores; 'Reg. S4D' is simply a shortened name. The diagnostic comparisons are unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 substantially revises LRA settings across five tasks. ListOps changes from 500 to 100 epochs and learning rate 0.002 to 0.01; Retrieval changes from 50 to 80 epochs; Pathfinder doubles features from 128 to 256 and batch size from 8 to 16. Text dropout and weight decay, and Path-X epochs, weight decay, and sampling-period range also change. These are revisions to previously stated settings.

E4.justification: The trained-versus-frozen initialization study, singular-value histograms, perturbation tests, impulse-response analysis, numerical-rank trials, and sampling-period sensitivity plots are retained. Their questions and evidence are unchanged; relabeling and moving them do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Table 1 extends uncertainty reporting to all six headline HOPE-SSM LRA results, specifying medians and standard deviations over five random seeds instead of unspecified point accuracies. v1 does not disclose its LRA run count, so this establishes new reporting rather than a known increase in runs. Existing supplementary trial counts and distribution summaries remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all six HOPE accuracies: ListOps 60.20 to 62.60, Text 89.60 to 89.83, Retrieval 91.52 to 91.80, Image 88.76 to 88.68, Pathfinder 94.89 to 95.73, and Path-X 96.84 to 98.45; the average changes from 86.97 to 87.85. Liquid S4 and S5 result rows are added. Changed settings and aggregation prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The four main theorems and their appendix proofs are substantively unchanged. Section 3 removes the separate reduced-order Hankel-norm approximation guarantee while retaining the transfer-function error bound. Section 4 also qualifies exponential memory decay as asymptotic, replacing v1's assertion of exponential decay at every positive lag.

C1.justification: The core contribution remains HOPE parameterization with robust initialization and training. The abstract and introduction now restrict non-decaying memory to a fixed time window, and the contribution list extends the performance claim beyond S4/S4D to other SSMs. It also strengthens the stated rank–performance relationship from a strong relationship to a causal one.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly warns that the three illustrative initialization schemes are not representative. Section 4 qualifies the parameter-count comparison by noting S4D variants that combine B and C or share A, restricting the one-third comparison to vanilla S4D. The finite memory-window limitation was already explained in v1, although v2 emphasizes it more prominently.

D1.justification: v2 adds step-by-step pseudocode in Algorithm 1, identifies AAA as the algorithm used for the existing init1 construction, and clarifies that NUFFT supports the derivation rather than appearing explicitly in the implementation. It also states a space bound and updates the documented hyperparameters. These additions clarify implementation without establishing a different HOPE procedure.

R1.justification: A dedicated Related Work discussion substantially expands positioning around direct convolution-kernel parameterization, discrete-time initialization, and memory/universality research, with six additional references. It distinguishes HOPE's continuous-dynamics approach from direct kernel methods and removes v1's criticism that HiPPO-LegS lacks the scaling required for its projection interpretation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of Sections 3–4 are rewritten to emphasize robust parameterization and numerical stability. Initialization descriptions move into a new Appendix C, the diagnostic narrative is reframed, and numbered subsections in Sections 4–5 become paragraph headings. This is substantial editorial restructuring despite the stable method.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is simplified and relocated; Figure 2 swaps its trained/frozen panels and changes the vertical scale; initialization labels change in Figures 2–4. Table 1 adds comparator and uncertainty rows and changes underlining from within-group best to overall second-best. Algorithm 1 adds a new display, while most figures retain their existing content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical transparency through five-seed uncertainty reporting and additional competitive baselines, while pseudocode and the AAA disclosure improve reproducibility. Qualifications on initialization examples and parameter savings improve precision. Changed LRA budgets and model widths limit interpretation of the higher scores, and stronger causal wording lacks new causal analysis. The net improvement is useful but incremental.
